question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{1}{5}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(\frac{4}{5})}^{x-1}(\frac{1}{5}), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=4) & =f(4) \\  & ={(\frac{4}{5})}^{3}(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{64}{625}.\end{aligned}
$$
